'''Rodney Michael Hood''' (born October 20, 1992) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] and [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] before declaring for the NBA Draft. Hood was drafted in [[2014 NBA Draft|2014]] by the [[Utah Jazz]]; and in 2018, he was dealt to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. He was then traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in 2019. He was then  traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in 2021. He signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] as a free agent for the 2021–2022 season before being traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] before the 2022 trade deadline.

==High school career==
Hood attended [[Meridian High School (Mississippi)|Meridian High School]] in the city of [[Meridian, Mississippi]]. As a junior in the 2009–10 season, he averaged 22.1 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 4.4 assists per game while leading the Wildcats to the Class 6A finals. Thus Meridian advanced past each school in the [[Mississippi High School Activities Association]]'s tournament, only to fall to Starkville in the championship game, 57–51.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=David |title=Starkville Captures Elusive State Title |url=https://www.cdispatch.com/sports/article.asp?aid=5132&TRID=1&TID= |access-date=17 November 2019 |work=[[The Commercial Dispatch]] |date=7 March 2010}}</ref>

As a senior, Hood posted averages of 24.8 points, 8.6 rebounds, 6.4 assists, 3.1 steals, and 2 blocks per contest, as he propelled Meridian to a 29–2 record and helped them capture a Class 6A championship. During the semifinals of that 2010–11 campaign, he tallied 27 points when Meridian defeated Starkville, 72–43; and in the title game against Vicksburg, he scored 24 points en route to the 62–47 victory.<ref name=bio>{{cite news|title=#5 Rodney Hood|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205700716|access-date=October 27, 2010|work=GoDuke.com|archive-date=October 11, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161011103419/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205700716|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Hood was ranked as the No. 5 [[small forward]] and the No. 16 player in the nation in 2011.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rodney Hood – Yahoo! Sports|url=https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Rodney-Hood-82490|access-date=October 27, 2010|work=Rivals.com}}</ref> In October 2010, he committed to Mississippi State University.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rodney Hood commits to Bulldogs|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=5733341|access-date=October 27, 2010|website=ESPN.com|date=October 27, 2010}}</ref>

Hood's childhood neighbor was [[Paramore]] lead singer [[Hayley Williams]]; Hood did not know this until March 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uproxx.com/dimemag/rodney-hood-childhood-neighbor-hayley-williams-paramore/|title=Rodney Hood Just Learned His Childhood Neighbor Was Hayley Williams|website=Uproxx.com|date=March 27, 2021|access-date=January 18, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]], Hood started in 29 of the 32 games that he played for the Bulldogs in [[2011–12 Mississippi State Bulldogs basketball team|2011–12]]. He was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman Team after averaging 10.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 2 assists per contest while shooting 44.3 percent from the field and 36.4 percent from three-point range.<ref name="bio" />

In July 2012, Rodney transferred to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Mississippi State's Rodney Hood makes Duke transfer official|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/acc/story/2012-07-05/duke-rodney-hood-mississippi-state-transfer/56037512/1|access-date=July 5, 2012|work=USAToday.com|date=July 5, 2012}}</ref> Despite having to sit out the [[2012–13 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2012–13 season]] in accordance with NCAA transfer rules, he consistently helped the team improve in practice and quickly established himself as one of the top players on the team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Meridian native Duke's Rodney Hood declares for NBA Draft|url=http://blog.gulflive.com/mississippi-press-sports/2014/04/meridian_native_dukes_rodney_h.html|access-date=April 18, 2014|work=Blogs.GulfLive.com|date=April 18, 2014}}</ref>

In his second year at Duke, he was selected as the team captain for the Blue Devil's [[2013–14 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2013–14]] campaign. The six-foot-eight small forward would play in 35 games, starting in 33 of them. He would average 16.1 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 2.1 assists in 32.9 minutes per game. He did so while shooting 46.4 percent from the field, including 42 percent from distance on the season. He earned second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) honors for his performance.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rodney Hood Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/rodney-hood-1.html|access-date=April 18, 2014|work=Sports-Reference.com}}</ref>

In April 2014, Hood declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite news|title=Duke forward Rodney Hood officially declares for the 2014 NBA Draft|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24531506/duke-forward-rodney-hood-officially-declares-for-the-2014-nba-draft|access-date=April 18, 2014|work=CBSSports.com|date=April 18, 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Utah Jazz (2014–2018)===
On June 26, 2014, Hood was selected with the 23rd pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-selects-exum-hood-2014-nba-draft|title=Jazz Selects Exum, Hood in 2014 NBA Draft|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2014|access-date=June 26, 2014}}</ref> later signing his rookie-scale contract with the team on July 11.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-signs-first-round-picks-dante-exum-and-rodney-hood|title=Jazz Signs First-Round Picks Danté Exum and Rodney Hood|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2014|access-date=July 11, 2014}}</ref> On March 16, 2015, he finished with a season-best 24 points after converting 9-of-11 shots from the field and 5-of-5 from behind the arc; thus he helped the Jazz beat the [[Charlotte Hornets]], 94–66, their sixth consecutive win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150316/CHAUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Jazz bury Hornets 94–66 with barrage of 3-pointers|work=NBA.com|date=March 16, 2015|access-date=March 16, 2015}}</ref>

Having solidified his role in the starting lineup, Hood started in all 79 of the games that he played in [[2015–16 Utah Jazz season|2015–16]]. He established himself as a go-to offensive option and reliable asset all around. Hood had 61 outings with double digits and 15 with 20-plus points.<ref>{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=Kristine|url=https://purpleandblues.com/2016/05/11/utah-jazz-player-review-rodney-hood/|title=Utah Jazz 2015–16 Review: Rodney Hood|work=purpleandblues.com|date=May 11, 2016|access-date=July 19, 2016}}</ref> On January 2, 2016, he posted a career-high 32 points against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] as the Jazz secured a 92–87 win in overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160102/MEMUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Hood scores 32 as Jazz beat Grizzlies 92–87 in OT|work=NBA.com|date=January 2, 2016|access-date=January 3, 2016}}</ref>

In the 2016–17 season opener on October 25, Hood added 26 points, to include a rim-rattling dunk and consecutive jumpers in the third quarter to give Utah a 77–71 lead, though the Jazz ultimately fell to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], 113–104.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899376|title=Lillard scores 39, Blazers run home-opening win streak to 16|work=ESPN.com|date=October 25, 2016|access-date=October 25, 2016}}</ref> On December 16, 2016, he hit the first game-clincher of his NBA career, pulling up for a three-pointer in transition with 0.8 seconds left; the shot secured a 103–100 victory over the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. He finished the contest with 15 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899840|title=Hood hits pull-up 3 to give Jazz 103–100 win over Mavericks|work=ESPN.com|date=December 16, 2016|access-date=December 17, 2016}}</ref> On January 13, 2017, he scored a season-high 27 points during a 110–77 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900021|title=Hood's season-high 27 lead Jazz to 110–77 win over Pistons|work=ESPN.com|date=January 13, 2017|access-date=January 14, 2017}}</ref> He recorded a new season-best 28 points on March 5 as the Jazz defeated the [[Sacramento Kings]], 110–109, in overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900326|title=Gobert's reviewed tip-in lifts Jazz past Kings in overtime|work=ESPN.com|date=March 5, 2017|access-date=March 6, 2017}}</ref>

In the 2017–18 campaign, Hood scored a season-high 25 points, 15 of which were in the third quarter, as he helped the Jazz rally and defeat the [[Dallas Mavericks]], 104–89, on October 30, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974849|title=Hood scores season high 25, Jazz beat Mavericks 104–89|work=ESPN.com|date=October 30, 2017|access-date=October 30, 2017}}</ref> On November 18,  during a 125–85 victory over the [[Orlando Magic]], he set a new season high with 31 points and did so coming off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974980|title=Jazz stop 3-game slide with 125–85 win over Magic|work=ESPN.com|date=November 18, 2017|access-date=November 19, 2017}}</ref> Hood did not finish the season with Utah before being traded.

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018–2019)===
[[File:Rodney Hood against the Portland Trail Blazers (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Hood with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in 2019]]
On February 8, 2018, Hood was acquired by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in a three-team trade that also involved the Jazz and the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/rhood-ghill-trade-180208|title=Cavaliers Acquire George Hill and Rodney Hood in Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018}}</ref> In his debut for the Cavaliers three days later, he scored 15 points during a 121–99 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975581|title=Truth is: Cavaliers beat Celtics 121–99 on Paul Pierce's day|work=ESPN.com|date=February 11, 2018|access-date=February 11, 2018}}</ref> 
On May 7, 2018, Hood refused to enter Game 4 vs the [[Toronto Raptors]] with the Cavaliers up 110–80 with 7:38 left in the 4th Quarter over frustrations relating to a lack of playing time. He later apologized.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23441765/rodney-hood-apologize-cleveland-cavaliers-refusing-enter-game| title = Rodney Hood to apologize to Cleveland Cavaliers for refusing to enter game| date = May 8, 2018}}</ref>
The Cavaliers made it to the [[2018 NBA Finals]], but would lose 4–0 to the [[Golden State Warriors]].

On September 10, 2018, Hood re-signed with the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cavs Re-Sign Rodney Hood |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/hood-signing-2018 |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 10, 2018 |date=September 10, 2018}}</ref> On October 30, in a 136–114 victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]], he scored a season-high 26 points to help snap Cleveland's six-game losing streak.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070778|title=Cavaliers end season-opening slide, beat Hawks 136–114|work=ESPN.com|date=October 30, 2018|access-date=October 30, 2018}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2019–2021)===
On February 4, 2019, Hood was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Nik Stauskas]], [[Wade Baldwin IV]], and two future second-round picks.<ref>{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ACQUIRE RODNEY HOOD|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-rodney-hood|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 4, 2019|date=February 4, 2019}}</ref> On March 3, 2019, he scored a season-high 27 points, all in the second half, in a 118–108 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071617|title=Hood, Nurkic lead Blazers past Hornets 118–108|work=ESPN.com|date=March 3, 2019|access-date=March 4, 2019}}</ref> In Game 6 of the Trail Blazers' second-round playoff series against the [[Denver Nuggets]], Hood scored a playoff career-high 25 points in a 119–108 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401129365|title=Blazers force Game 7 with 119–108 victory over Denver|work=ESPN.com|date=May 9, 2019|access-date=May 9, 2019}}</ref> For the third consecutive season all with different teams, Hood was eliminated from the playoffs in a 4-game sweep by the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/blazers-news-rodney-hood-swept-warriors-past-three-seasons/|title=Blazers' Rodney Hood has now been swept by the Warriors in the past three seasons|date=May 20, 2019}}</ref> On December 6, 2019, the Trail Blazers announced that Hood would be out for the rest of the 2019–2020 season and may miss the start of next season as well since he incurred a torn left [[Achilles tendon|Achilles]] during a 136–113 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|first1=Casey|last1=Holdahl|title=Hood Ruptures Left Achilles, Likely Out For The Season|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/forwardcenter/hood-ruptures-left-achilles-likely-out-season|date=December 6, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 6, 2019}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2021)===
On March 25, 2021, Hood along with [[Gary Trent Jr.]] were traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Norman Powell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-acquire-trent-jr-and-hood-portland|title=Raptors Acquire Trent Jr. and Hood from Portland|publisher=Toronto Raptors|date=March 25, 2021|access-date=March 25, 2021}}</ref> On August 3, he was waived by the Raptors.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Scott|last=Rafferty|title=Toronto Raptors waive DeAndre' Bembry, Rodney Hood and Paul Watson|url=https://ca.nba.com/news/toronto-raptors-waive-deandre-bembry-rodney-hood-and-paul-watson/1pbb39v7cfky91pcqskber8ug0|website=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2021–2022)===
On August 6, 2021, Hood signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on a one-year, veteran's minimum contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Three Players|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-three-players|website=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021|access-date=August 6, 2021}}</ref> On December 12, Hood scored a season high 14 points, while shooting 100% from the field, in a 112–97 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202112120NYK.html|title=Milwaukee Bucks at New York Knicks Box Score, December 12, 2021|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 18, 2022}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2022)===
On February 10, 2022, Hood was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] as part of a four-team trade.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-finalize-four-team-trade-send-ibaka-milwaukee|title=LA Clippers Finalize Four-Team Trade, Send Ibaka To Milwaukee|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2022}}</ref>

===Memphis Hustle (2024)===
On February 11, 2024, Hood joined the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Memphis Hustle|title=happy to have you fam 🤝 @rodneyhood|number=1756710255507955904|user=MemphisHustle|date=February 11, 2024|access-date=February 12, 2024}}</ref>

On November 21, 2024, Hood announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Rodney Hood Announces Retirement|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/11/rodney-hood-announces-retirement.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=November 21, 2024|access-date=November 22, 2024}}</ref>

==National team career==
In July 2016, Hood joined the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States men's]] select team to train with the [[2016 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2016 Olympic team]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rodney Hood Chosen to 2016 USA Men's Select Team |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/rodney-hood-chosen-2016-usa-mens-select-team |access-date=2023-03-11 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref>

In November 2022, Hood was chosen to represent Team USA in the second round of the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Americas)|2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-30 |title=USA Basketball picks next World Cup qualifying roster |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-basketball-colombia-brazil-philippines-0692cb6288008b634dc63948a3eae8cc |access-date=2023-03-11 |website=AP NEWS |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On January 3, 2016, Hood's fiancé, Richa Jackson, gave birth to the couple's first child, a son.<ref>{{cite web|first=Aaron|last=Falk|title=Jazz notes: Rodney Hood's son born six weeks early|url=http://www.sltrib.com/home/3378873-155/jazz-notes-rodney-hoods-son-born|work=SLTrib.com|publisher=The Salt Lake Tribune|date=January 4, 2016|access-date=January 4, 2016}}</ref> On July 29, Hood married Jackson in [[Oklahoma City, Oklahoma]].

On April 18, 2018, Jackson gave birth to a set of twins named Rich and Riley, respectively.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mom |first1=Team |title=Get to Know Rodney Hood Ahead of His First Game with the Blazers |url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2019/2/7/18209937/nba-trade-rumors-portland-trail-blazers-rodney-hood-skal-labissiere-cavs-kings#:~:text=For%20the%20last%20four%20summers,series%20against%20the%20Indiana%20Pacers. |website=Blazer's Edge |publisher=The Salt Lake Tribune |access-date=9 December 2024}}</ref>
